The output current is about 3× the input (5.97e-5 / 2e-5 ≈ 2.99, i.e. +198.6% error). That matches the netlist: M2 has effective width W·m = 19.28 × 3 = 57.84 against M1's 20.23, a ratio of about 2.86. Output resistance also drops from the spec's 330 kΩ to 222 kΩ, consistent with M2 carrying roughly three times the reference current. The compliance voltage is unaffected, as expected since the device geometry is the same. M1 is the only other device, and it is the diode-connected reference that sets the input current, so it is the next candidate.

Note that M2's W = 19.28 µm differs slightly from M1's 20.23 µm, which by itself would give about 4.7% error at ratio 1. That is inside the 5% limit but close to it, so the original design may have intended matched widths.
